blocks.source: Source: MLS® data from the Greater Vancouver REALTORS® and the Fraser Valley Real Estate Board, compiled by SnapStats®. Rank counts only communities with at least ten homes listed. Falling listings with steady sales mean homes are being absorbed faster; rising listings with steady sales mean more choice for buyers. A sellers’ best bet is a community where homes sell quickly against the number listed; a buyers’ best bet is the reverse. Sales ratio is homes sold divided by homes listed. On the reports’ own scale under 12% is a buyers’ market, 12% to 20% is balanced and over 20% is a sellers’ market. With fewer than ten homes listed, one sale moves the ratio a long way, so treat it as a rough signal.

blocks.text: Between June 2026 and October 2026, detached houses: listings fell from 106 in June to 89 in October (−16.0%), and it took 11.0% of the city’s 464 sales over the period; condos and townhomes: listings fell from 121 in June to 107 in October (−11.6%), and it took 6.9% of the city’s 737 sales over the period.
The monthly write-ups singled out West Newton for detached houses in September (a sellers’ best bet); condos and townhomes in June, July, August, September (a buyers’ best bet).

items.t: Lot fabric: single-family houses on the residential streets west of King George Boulevard are the typical form; apartment buildings concentrate at Newton Town Centre on the east side of King George Blvd; industrial land sits in the Highway 99 portion of the plan area, which is not housing. A "land" purchase on the residential streets is therefore normally an existing house lot, not a vacant new-subdivision lot. No typical lot size, lot count or lot price is stated — none is documented on an official source for this sub-area.

Fee-simple lots are the default form: the confirmed house stock is fee-simple — the buyer's own title, no strata corporation, no Form B, no strata fees. Strata in the area is mainly the town-centre apartment form. A sub-area-wide strata-versus-freehold split is not verified — no official source publishes one.
: a bare-land strata lot IS strata tenure on the lot itself — Form B, strata fees and registered bylaws apply to the lot; it is NOT fee-simple.

Industrial ground — Highway 99 area, documented as a land class only: the southern part of the plan area is the Highway 99 industrial area, zoned in the industrial zones under Zoning Bylaw No. 12000 per the City plan. A buyer near that edge must verify neighbouring uses and truck routes.

Assemblies / development sites, documented AS SUCH, never as inventory: the live feed showed a multi-lot development assembly on 122a Street whose listing text cites RA zoning and a transit-oriented-area designation — that is listing-card text only, cited as feed evidence that assembly marketing reaches this page; it is not verified zoning, not a City-confirmed proposal, and not lot inventory here. No other assembly, development site or rezoning proposal is documented in this sub-area's research.
Named buildings — cross-reference ONLY, never land

ALR vs non-ALR / flood split: the residential upland portion is outside the Serpentine & Nicomekl lowland floodplain; the south end falls toward those dyke-protected lowlands, and ALR land lies south and west toward the lowlands. No parcel-level split is published — a specific property's ALR status is checked in the ALC maps and its flood position on the City's flood mapping.

Serviced vs unserviced: the research documents no well/septic pocket on the residential streets; properties not connected to community water and sewer are an SSMUH exemption category, which is the servicing check for any edge parcel — servicing for a specific lot is not confirmed until confirmed with the City.
: No phase selling vacant lots is documented in West Newton. Never mixed with built presales (Harth above).

items.t: West Newton is the board sub-area and City plan area covering the Newton lands west of King George Boulevard toward the Delta border (Scott Road / 120 Street side), including the Highway 99 industrial area at the south.

Nearby areas, per the research: East Newton (east, across King George Boulevard), Scottsdale / North Delta (west, across Scott Road), Bear Creek Green Timbers (north), and the Serpentine & Nicomekl lowlands (south). Newton Town Centre, at King George Blvd / 72 Ave, is the town-centre core at the area's east edge.
Sub-area medians are not published (Not verified at sub-area level). Surrey community — Detached: 1,120 / 84 / median $1,215,000; combined attached: 1,523 / 114 / median $512,944.

Scott Elementary, 7079 148 St (ESTABLISHED CORRECTION: NOT 7075 124 St); Bear Creek Elementary, 13780 80 Ave; Frank Hurt Secondary, 13940 77 Ave (level read from its name — the Ministry level field mislabels it). Which of these fall inside the board sub-area line is not verified (no public board boundary); Frank Hurt is carried as the recorded catchment secondary for the sample address below, not as a school inside the sub-area.
Settled locator chain, single-address only, non-transferable: sample address 7079 148 St → T.E. Every other West Newton address's catchment is not verified.

Transit: the R1 RapidBus on King George Boulevard (Newton Exchange to Guildford Exchange); the R6 Scott Road RapidBus on the west edge (Scott Road Station to Newton Exchange); routes 323 (via 124 St) and 364 (via 64 Ave) through the area.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect land buyers in West Newton

items.t: Secondary suites (Bylaw No. 12000, rules-gaps verified): one secondary suite may be permitted per single family, semi-detached or duplex dwelling unit; a suite is not permitted within a coach house or garden suite; a suite's habitable floor area may not exceed 40% of the principal dwelling unit; no 90 m² cap was found in the current consolidated text; a suite is not a separate strata lot.

Streamside / flood diligence: Surrey's streamside setbacks are defined in Part 7A of Zoning Bylaw No. 12000 and vary by stream class, with the Sensitive Ecosystems Development Permit process alongside — no single riparian figure is stated for any lot here. Separately, south-end lots fall toward the Serpentine & Nicomekl lowlands: confirm the specific lot against the City's flood mapping and ask about flood insurance before subjects.

ALR block (south/west edge parcels only, where a parcel IS in the ALR): subdivision within the ALR requires ALC approval; ALR residences cannot be stratified (ALC Bulletin 09 s.6; SPA s.239; ALCA s.21(1)); caps: principal ≤500 m², suite within principal only, additional residence 90 m² (≤40 ha) / 186 m² (>40 ha). Farm class is three-tier — $2,500 on 0.8–4 ha / $2,500 + 5% of value over 4 ha / $10,000 under 0.8 ha, applications by Oct 31 — a flat "$2,500+" line is an ERROR, and no farm-class claim is asserted for West Newton.

items.t: The park is small, and that is the supply: Newton Mobile Home Park has 34 home sites (directory-stated) on the area's main corridor — for a buyer set on the 55+ park form in West Newton, turnover, not a large resale pool, is the supply, and the record behind it is a directory entry plus listing statements, not an operator's disclosure.

West Newton South no longer exists as a plan: The City states that part of the West Newton NCP set was rescinded by the Surrey 2050 OCP update (Bylaw 21900, adopted Jun 15, 2026) — density or use claims near the park should be checked against the current OCP and Zoning Bylaw 12000, not the old plan.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect duplexes in West Newton

items.t: Zoning, SSMUH and suites (Surrey): Zoning Bylaw No. 12000 governs (residential zones R1–R6 in the neighbourhood portion; industrial zones in the Highway 99 industrial area; streamside setbacks sit in Part 7A of Zoning 12000 and vary by stream class — no single riparian figure is ever stated). SSMUH (Jul 8, 2024 frame): A maximum of 3 units on lots smaller than 280 m², 4 units on lots larger than 280 m², and up to 6 units on eligible lots of at least 281 m² within 400 m of a frequent bus stop; one secondary suite per house under the BC Building Code; properties not connected to community water and sewer are among the exemptions. Duplexes are the baseline SSMUH form. The Surrey suite rule is its own: A secondary suite is capped at 40% of the principal dwelling's habitable area — never borrowed for another city. The SSMUH changes do not retroactively legalize suites built without permits — verify a suite's permit status before marketing its income. Servicing Bylaw 8830 (1986) is verified. Surrey has no Supreme Court registry.

Flood and ALR: The south end of West Newton falls toward the Serpentine & Nicomekl lowlands — the dyke-protected floodplain south of Newton — while the residential upland portion is outside that lowland floodplain; ALR land lies south and west toward the lowlands, and a specific property's ALR and flood status is checked parcel by parcel (ALC maps; City flood mapping) before subjects come off. Homes near the Highway 99 industrial edge also need a neighbouring-uses and truck-route check.

blocks.text: Sources

faq.q: Is the 122a Street assembly a lot I can buy?
faq.a: Verify any assembly claim against the current OCP (Bylaw 21900) and Zoning Bylaw 12000 with the City.

faq.q: How many units can my lot hold?
faq.a: 3 units under 280 m², 4 over 280 m², up to 6 on eligible lots of 281 m²+ within 400 m of a frequent bus stop — and SSMUH does not retroactively legalize unpermitted suites. Confirm band and eligibility with the City.

faq.q: Should I worry about flood or ALR on a south-end lot?
faq.a: Check both, don't assume: the south end falls toward the dyke-protected Serpentine & Nicomekl lowlands while the residential upland is outside that floodplain, and ALR land lies south and west toward the lowlands. Confirm the lot on City flood mapping and in the ALC maps.

faq.q: Is the industrial edge a problem for a nearby lot?
faq.a: It is a diligence item, not a verdict: verify neighbouring uses, truck routes and the residential/industrial zone line for any parcel near the Highway 99 area.

faq.q: Is my lot fee-simple or strata?
faq.a: The house fabric is fee-simple by default and no bare-land strata plan in West Newton was verified — but tenure is read off title per parcel, and a bare-land strata lot, if one surfaces, is strata tenure with Form B, fees and bylaws.

faq.q: What mobile/manufactured homes can I buy in West Newton?
faq.a: Its record rests on a park directory plus MLS listing statements; no operator source was read, so park-level details are confirmed with the park, not from listings.

faq.q: Do I own the land at Newton Mobile Home Park?
faq.a: No. You own the home (a chattel) and rent the pad — that is not land ownership. There are no strata fees and no Form B; the tenancy runs under the MHPTA, the pad tenancy agreement and the park rules, and the purchase is subject to park approval.

faq.q: How much can my pad rent go up?
faq.a: Once every 12 months, on at least 3 full months' notice, by inflation plus the park's proportional levy/utility amount: 2.3% + proportional for 2026, 2.2% + proportional for 2027 (RTB, verified Nov 1, 2026).

faq.q: Can the park refuse my purchase because of age?
faq.a: In a 55+ park, in effect yes: assignment needs the park owner's consent on RTB Form 10 (response by the 10th day, silence deemed consent, no fee for consent), and the provincial assignment rules recognise the park's 55+ reservation (at least one of 2+ tenants aged 55+, Human Rights Code s.10(2)(b)(i) framework). The seller must give you the written tenancy agreement and park rules before consent is requested — get both.

faq.q: The old West Newton South plan shows more density — can I rely on it?
faq.a: No. West Newton South was rescinded by the Surrey 2050 OCP update (Bylaw 21900) and is no longer in effect; confirm any density or use claim against the current OCP and Zoning Bylaw 12000.

faq.q: What south-end checks matter before subjects come off?
faq.a: The floodplain check (the land falls toward the dyke-protected Serpentine & Nicomekl lowlands), the ALR check on the ALC maps, and a neighbouring-uses check near the Highway 99 industrial area.

T.E. Scott Elementary (7079 148 St) is in the plan area, Bear Creek Elementary (13780 80 Ave) is at its north edge, and Frank Hurt Secondary (13940 77 Ave) is the area secondary; catchments are by address through the SD36 School Locator.

The City's West Newton plan covers the area west of King George Boulevard including the Highway 99 industrial lands; the Newton Town Centre Plan covers the King George / 72 Avenue core; and the Surrey 2050 OCP update rescinded West Newton South.
